description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING.  The area is
USER-PARKED (pack/unpack, 2026-09-06), so this is filed with the full oracle
rather than fixed.

`pack`/`unpack`'s `U` format is implemented as UTF-8 OCTETS in BOTH
directions, which round-trips through itself and diverges from perl at both
boundaries.  perl's `U` is CHARACTER mode when the template STARTS with it
(perl's own default, `U0`); `C0` is the byte mode that decodes/encodes UTF-8.

THE ORACLE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, every row measured; hex):

  template / argument                perl        PCL         verdict
  unpack "U*",   "\xC4\x84"          (C4,84)     (104)       PCL WRONG
  unpack "C0U*", "\xC4\x84"          (104)       (104)       agree
  unpack "U0U*", "\xC4\x84"          (C4,84)     (C4,84)     agree
  unpack "C0U*", "\x{104}"           (4)         (4)         agree
  unpack "aU*",  "\xC4\x84"          (0,0)       (0,4)       PCL WRONG
  unpack "C*", pack("U",0x104)       (104)       (C4,84)     PCL WRONG
  unpack "U*", pack("U",0x104)       (104)       (104)       agree (round trip)

  unpack "U*", "\x{1234}"            (1234)      (4)         PCL WRONG
  unpack "U*", "a\x{1234}b"          (61,1234,62)(61,122)    PCL WRONG

WHERE: `cl/pack-impl.pl`.  `_unpack_utf8_char` (line ~769) decodes UTF-8
octets unconditionally, and PCL strings are SBCL CHARACTER vectors -- so for
`"\x{1234}"` it reads `ord` = 0x1234, takes the `>= 0xF0` branch, and returns
`0x1234 & 0x07` = 4.  That is the observed `4`.  The pack side is the `$ch eq
'U'` arm at line ~672 plus the `$utf8_mode` pre-encode at ~1173.

THE FIX SHAPE: the DEFAULT `U` arm is `ord(substr($s,$i++,1))` -- i.e. exactly
the `W` arm without its 0..255 clamp -- and the octet-decoding
`_unpack_utf8_char` belongs to `C0` mode only.  The mode plumbing already
exists (`my $utf8_mode = ($tmpl =~ s/^U0//)`), but it currently means "encode
the SOURCE to UTF-8 first", which is why `U0U*` agrees with perl by a
round-trip rather than by modelling the mode; expect to re-read what `U0`/`C0`
mean before moving the arm (perldoc -f pack, "U0 mode ... is the default for U
as the first format").

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/sprintf.t` rows 21, 22, 23 -- the [perl #6769] block
`sprintf "%x %d", unpack("U*", $a), length($a)` -- are this and nothing else
(the strings themselves are right: `length` and `ord` both agree with perl).
op/pack.t's own `U` rows are attributed to the parking.

BAR WHEN IT IS FIXED: `tools/rebuild-pack` + `perl tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl
--jobs 1 --timeout 380 perl-tests/pack.t` + `tools/sweep-diff.pl` (expect 0
new), because cl/pcl-pack.lisp is a checked-in transpiled artifact.
subject: pack/unpack "U" is UTF-8 OCTETS in both directions where perl default is CHARACTER mode -- unpack "U*","\x{1234}" is (1234) in perl and (4) in PCL; 7-row oracle table (pack/unpack PARKED)
